launches.body:
**Hey everyone!**

We're Vishnu and Chrisvin, the co-founders of Tepali.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zt2O8-s3Alo>

**TL;DR**

Tepali is the AI EMR for medspas & wellness clinics. Front desk, charting, point of sale, and marketing in one system, with an AI employee that books new leads, charts every appointment, and brings past clients back.

**The problem**

A medspa runs on ten to twelve disconnected tools: one for booking, another for charting, another for payments, texting, marketing, and inventory. None of them talk to each other. The gaps between them get filled with the owner's time: missed calls, after-hours charting, and leads that go cold before anyone follows up.

Most of that software was built for salons, before AI. Even the all-in-one platforms digitize the manual work instead of doing it.

**What Tepali does**

First, one system for the whole practice: front desk, EMR, point of sale, and marketing. Scheduling, the client record, charts, consent forms, inventory, payments, memberships, and every text, call, and Instagram DM live in the same place.

Then an AI employee that works across all of it, at every stage of the visit:

**Before the visit, it books new leads.** It answers every call and text 24/7. Leads from ads, Instagram DMs, and website forms get a reply in seconds, and it converses with each one until they book a consultation. Every conversation lands in one unified inbox, so your front desk sees the whole thread.

**During the visit, it charts every appointment.** An ambient scribe listens to the treatment and writes a complete, service-specific chart as it happens, so charts are done without taking up provider time. Charting is built for injectables: injection maps on the client's own before photos, consent forms sent automatically, Good Faith Exam tracking, and inventory deducted by unit and lot.

**After the visit, it brings past clients back.** It reaches out to clients who are due for their next treatment, recovers no-shows, fills cancellations from the waitlist, and requests reviews. Checkout fills the cart from the visit, with memberships, packages, gift cards, and card readers at the counter.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98330&key=user_uploads/2145173/726ff95e-085c-4c19-8c27-bfeb944afc36)

**Who it's for**

Medspas and aesthetics practices (injectables, lasers, skin), and wellness clinics: IV therapy, medical weight loss, hormone therapy, peptides, and longevity. All are cash-pay medical businesses that need charting, consent, and inventory tracking.

**The team**

We're best friends who grew up together and have spent our careers inside this exact problem.

Vishnu studied CS at Carnegie Mellon and led engineering at MealPal (Series B). At Dripos (YC S20), he built the all-in-one point of sale used by thousands of coffee shops and saw how much a service business changes when its software finally works as one system.

Chrisvin studied at NYU Stern and executed $30B in M&A at PJT Partners. He then scaled operations at Rilla, a vertical AI unicorn, where he saw what happens when AI is applied to high-ticket service industries.

**Get in touch**

Own or operate a medspa or wellness clinic? Book a demo → [tepali.com](http://tepali.com)

Know a medspa owner? Intro us → [founders@tepali.com](mailto:founders@tepali.com)

launches.tagline: Meet Cumulus, the GPU cloud where you’re charged by physical resource usage for 50-70% savings.
launches.body:
## **TL;DR**

Cumulus is a performant GPU cloud that preemptively optimizes your training and inference workloads across our global supply of multi-tenant clusters. The result: we **save you 50-70%** through charging by physical resources used, provide faster inference with ultra-low cold starts, and ensure zero time spent debugging infrastructure.

**Ask**: If you’re training models or serving inference workloads, frustrated with GPU costs and performance, let us optimize your **LLMs, LoRAs, vision models, and more.**

**Website:** <https://cumuluslabs.io>\
**Docs:** <https://docs.cumuluslabs.io>

Launch Video: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=duQwV50GKXc>

## **The Problem**

AI teams are bleeding money and time on GPU infrastructure:

* **Massive waste**: Teams pay for idle GPUs sitting at 30-40% utilization because scaling is unpredictable
* **Infrastructure hell**: Engineers spend weeks configuring Kubernetes, debugging OOM errors, and managing failovers instead of building models
* **Cold start latency**: Inference workloads take 10-30+ seconds to spin up, killing user experience
* **Vendor lock-in**: Once you commit to a cloud provider, switching costs make it nearly impossible to optimize for price or performance
* **Skyrocketing costs**: Companies burn through runway 2-3x faster than planned because GPU bills spiral out of control

Every hour debugging infrastructure is an hour not spent improving your models. Every dollar wasted on idle GPUs is a dollar not spent on growth.

---

## **The Solution**

**Cumulus is a GPU optimization layer that makes compute cheap, fast, and invisible.**

We aggregate compute from everywhere—big cloud providers, trusted data centers, individual hosts—into a single unified pool. Then we do three things no one else does:

# **1. Predictive Packing & Live Migration (Training/Fine-tuning)**

Your training jobs are intelligently packed alongside other workloads to maximize GPU utilization. As your job runs, we predict resource usage and **live-migrate you to faster or cheaper clusters** without interruption. No more paying for an entire H100 when you only need 40% of it.

# **2. Execution State Capture & Global CDN (Inference)**

We capture your model's live execution state (VRAM, memory, loaded weights) and replicate it across our global compute CDN. When a request comes in, we serve from the closest cluster with **ultra fast cold starts**—no more waiting 30 seconds for a job to spin up. We have tested with **LLMs, vision models, LORAs, and many others.**

# **3. Intelligent Scheduling & Auto-Recovery**

Our scheduler constantly monitors your jobs, diagnoses failures, and auto-recovers without manual intervention. The Cumulus prediction system learns your usage patterns over time and pre-allocates resources before you need them.

**The bottom line:** _You write 20 lines of config. We handle everything else._

Our Demo: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J0KRFWE3-fg>

launches.body:
Hi everyone, we’re Evan and Jad — two Dartmouth grads building Verdex.

**TL;DR:** Verdex replaces manual inspections in insurance with real-time digital audits. We use high-resolution satellite imagery to help insurers verify and settle claims without ever leaving their desks, starting with crop insurance.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otKHPaRs-mQ>

### The Problem

Crop insurers worldwide spend over **$5 billion every year** on a single manual task: verification.

* Today, insurers cannot verify a claim without physically sending an adjuster to a field.
* This manual process is so slow and labor-intensive that it consumes nearly **10% of every premium dollar** collected globally.
* As extreme weather events increase, the volume of claims is skyrocketing, making the current adjuster model completely unscalable.

### The Solution

Verdex allows insurers to monitor every field on earth in real time.

* We combine high-resolution satellite imagery with local weather models to interpret field-level conditions with precision.
* Instead of waiting weeks for a field visit, insurers can verify the insured asset in seconds and settle the claim instantly. This means insurers aren’t scrambling to dispatch adjusters, and policyholders get paid on the spot.
* Last month, major regulators such as the USDA updated their guidelines to allow for satellite-based remote verification.

We are already live with one of the largest crop insurers in the US, helping them insure **100+ million acres** — that’s over **11% of all farmland** in the US. But insurance is more than just crops — our vision is to be the data and interpretability layer for any insurable asset you can see from space. We’re building the infrastructure to automate the verification process across insurance sectors like agriculture, property, and energy.

### Our Ask

We are looking for intros to insurers in agriculture, property, and energy.

If you have a lead or want to see a demo, reach out at [**founders@verdexai.com**](mailto:founders@verdexai.com)!

launches.body:
Hey YC!

We’re [Rithvik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rithvik-vanga-0824a5225/), [Alex](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alex-blackwell-506228206/), and [Tarun](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tarunvedula/), the team behind [Zatanna](https://www.linkedin.com/company/usezatanna/).

**TL;DR:** Today, most AI companies rely on slow, brittle, and unreliable computer-use agents to interact with software that has no API.  Zatanna solves this with faster, cheaper, and more reliable APIs for AI agents by reverse engineering requests and taking care of antibot infrastructure. 

[Video Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HUCOKVn-atM)

**The Problem:**

A huge amount of valuable business software still has no usable API. So when AI companies need their agents to interact with ERPs, PMS systems, portals, marketplaces, or other operational websites, they often fall back to browser automation.

That means the agent is stuck looking at screens, clicking buttons, waiting for pages to load, dealing with logins, handling UI changes, and breaking every time the workflow shifts. It is fine for showing that something is possible. It is terrible when the workflow actually matters.

Teams end up spending an absurd amount of engineering time maintaining brittle browser automations instead of building product and serving customers.

**The Solution:**

Zatanna runs these workflows at the request layer.

We observe how a workflow works once, reconstruct the underlying request sequence, and host it as a clean API that any agent can call. Instead of navigating a browser, the agent just hits an endpoint.

That makes the workflow:

* faster
* cheaper
* more reliable
* much easier to maintain at scale

We also handle the painful infrastructure required to keep these workflows alive in production:

* session and credential management
* request sequencing
* proxy networks and traffic distribution
* retries, monitoring, and recovery

Today we’re already supporting customers where either throughput or reliability is mission-critical, from high-volume consumer platforms to operationally sensitive industries like logistics.

**Where we’re seeing this most:**

* ERPs like SAP
* PMS / POS systems
* insurance/benefits/claims portals
* marketplaces(checkout flows)
* operational websites with no APIs
* basically anywhere the current solution is scraping or browser automation

**Why we’re doing this:**

We started in vertical AI and ran into this problem ourselves. The model layer kept getting easier. Software access was the real bottleneck. A huge amount of engineering effort went into keeping integrations alive instead of improving the actual agent.

So we decided to build the thing we wished we had.

**What we’re looking for:**

If you’re building something that depends on browser automation or computer-use agents for integrations, especially where reliability, speed, or cost matter, we’d love to take a look at the workflow.

Book a call [here](https://zatanna.cal.com/tarun/30min?user=tarun&overlayCalendar=true) or email [**tarun@zatanna.ai**](mailto:tarun@zatanna.ai)

launches.body:
👋 We're Nars and Nishant, founders of Skillsync (W26).

**TL;DR:** Skillsync lets you move your context (sessions, memory, and skills) across every coding agent you use, with nothing lost. Start in Claude Code, continue in Codex, sync it with your team. Say it once; every agent & teammate has it.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=112177&key=user_uploads/2980881/daf33474-9f03-4b30-ae87-d2d5de4efb88)

AI chats are annoying. Your context is trapped inside whatever agent you're using. You plan everything out in the Claude app, then open Claude Code to build, and none of that thinking comes with you. Switch from Claude Code to Cursor or Codex and it's the same story: you start from zero, re-explaining everything. And sharing your best skills with your team means zip files and Slack messages nobody can find.

Skillsync is a **local-first desktop app** that frees your context from any single agent:

* 🔁 **Move a session between agents with nothing lost**, including the full conversation, reasoning, and tool history.
* 🧠 **KYC: Know Your Context.** Keep your skills and memory in one place, searchable from any agent via MCP.
* 👥 **Sync your skills across your team**, edit once and everyone stays current. No zip files, no stale copies.

Everything runs on your machine, so your context stays yours.

We spent years building open source payments infra that connected dozens of payment processors, and scaled it to 30k+ GitHub stars. Making all those systems talk to each other taught us what real interoperability takes.

**One more thing…** 

The hard part, the engine that translates sessions across different agent formats without losing anything, is **open source**. It's written in Rust and it's called **txcript:** <https://github.com/skillsynchq/txcript/>. Don't take our word for it: **read the code**.

We're on a mission to set your context free. If this resonates, try Skillsync at <https://skillsync.com>

You can also reach us at [founders@skillsync.com](mailto:founders@skillsync.com)

launches.title: RoboDock: Autonomous Depots for Autonomous Fleets
launches.tagline: Robots that automate depot operations for AV fleets.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Autonomous vehicles are scaling fast, but the depots that charge, inspect, and operate them are still manual. RoboDock automates charging and vehicle inspections so fleets can finally be end-to-end autonomous.

<https://youtu.be/hNc56Z1-Ojs>

🚧 **The problem**

Autonomous vehicles are no longer the bottleneck. **Infrastructure is.**

By 2035, there will be \~76M autonomous vehicles globally, and the AV market is expected to grow from \~$200B today to \~$3T.

Yet the depots that power these fleets are still manually run. If you were to go watch one, you’d be shocked at how many people it takes to maintain the vehicles.

Today, AV and EV fleet depots rely on people to:

* Plug and unplug vehicles into chargers
* Catch missed or failed charge events
* Manually inspect vehicles before and after deployment
* Maintain road-readiness under tight turnaround times

This breaks the autonomy loop.

The pain these fleets experience?

* \~$900k per depot per year in charging labor and overhead
* Redundant chargers and vehicles to compensate for human error
* 2–3 year timelines and $8M+ CapEx just to build new depots
* Vehicle downtime from missed issues and reactive maintenance (up to $650k per depot per year) → less time making money on the road

**Autonomous fleets can drive themselves, but they still can’t operate themselves.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97957&key=user_uploads/2727198/c431cd46-f80c-45da-982a-55bbc39ea137)

✅ **The solution**

**RoboDock is building autonomous depots for autonomous fleets.**

We deploy a robotic system that:

* Physically plugs vehicles into chargers
* Verifies successful charge initiation
* Performs automated post-trip vehicle inspections every time a vehicle returns

Our system works with **existing depots, existing chargers, and any vehicle type**. No layout changes and no rebuilds necessary.

Charging and inspections become:

* Fully autonomous
* Safe and consistent
* Closed-loop and self-optimizing

We’re turning depots from manual cost centers into **self-running infrastructure.**

**🧠 Why RoboDock**

* **Hardware-first autonomy**: We automate the physical work that actually limits fleet scale
* **Robotic charging**: No humans, no missed plugs, no idle vehicles
* **Safety-first inspections**: Vision + thermal sensing catch issues humans can’t see consistently
* **Retrofit, not rebuild**: Deploy into live depots with zero operational disruption
* **Designed for scale**: Every vehicle, every return, every day improves the system

This is how autonomy actually becomes autonomous.

**👩🏾‍🔧👩🏻‍💻 Our team**

We’ve spent our engineering careers building real-world autonomy. We met seven years ago at Stanford, when Zinny was Celine’s TA.

**Zinny Weli — CEO & Co-Founder**

Led design and deployment of autonomous charging systems for electric drones at Zipline, and designed the charging system for Amazon's first home robot and its advanced robotics manipulation platform.

**Celine Wang — CTO & Co-Founder**

Former vehicle platform engineer at Plus, where she retrofitted autonomous systems onto semi-truck fleets by integrating mechanical, electrical, and software stacks end-to-end. 

Together, we bring deep experience deploying autonomy where it actually breaks: the real world.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97957&key=user_uploads/2727198/78d912fd-def0-446f-91a6-d14d86babb5b)

**🙏 Our ask**

We’re onboarding early pilot partners and would love introductions to:

* AV & EV fleet operators
* Infrastructure, parking, and depot operations team
* Ports, logistics yards, and large fleet facilities
* Hardware and systems minded investors thinking about autonomy at scale
* Robotics/computer vision engineers

If you’re thinking about how fleets operate, we should talk! Email [zinny@robodock.tech](mailto:zinny@robodock.tech) or [celine@robodock.tech](mailto:celine@robodock.tech).

launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re Ab, Sam and Zac.

**We are building the logistics infrastructure to modernize healthcare operations, beginning with physician scheduling and care coordination, to combat rampant inefficiencies in healthcare.**

[**https://youtu.be/SXIaP6D1PJo?si=ERtC2Uq2_l92gqbS**](https://youtu.be/SXIaP6D1PJo?si=ERtC2Uq2_l92gqbS)

**Our Beginning:**

This all began when a doctor at Johns Hopkins told us that residents and attending physicians spend **hundreds of hours** each year scheduling. Thus began our **physician** **scheduling service**. 

We built an internal **Optimization Programming Language** that lets us create complex schedules far faster than traditional methods. Our clients now review schedules we build, rather than spend hundreds of hours manually creating them.

Through our scheduling, we have built trust in healthcare logistics across major academic health systems with active contracts at **Mass General**, **Johns Hopkins**, **UT Southwestern**, **LA General**, **UCF** and more! We are actively growing and onboarding new partners.

**Revelations I:**

These relationships revealed that healthcare administration, more generally, is unbelievably manual, disjointed, and inefficient. That’s why we have expanded our scope to tackle clinical care coordination. We have separated clinic operations into two segments: **The Patients**, and **The Resources**. 

**The Patients:**

The patient journey at most clinics begins with a referral process that leads to a triaging bottleneck before a patient can be seen. Only once this is complete can the complex systems for evaluation and treatment tracking begin.

**The Resources:**

Managing and tracking personnel, rooms, and time is difficult for even the best administrative teams.

**The Secret**

The problem with healthcare is not on the demand side, it is on the supply side. **Care coordination is the bridge between patient needs and hospital resources.**

**Revelations II:**

With our design partners at **UCSF and other major healthcare systems**, we are building patient triaging and provider management systems to improve and automate care coordination, while reducing administrative burden.

We aim to modernize healthcare operations. As our partnerships grow and our scope expands, we will become the key player in **bringing healthcare operations into the future.**

**The Team**

We are a team of award-winning mathematicians, computer scientists, and logistics experts from Johns Hopkins University.

Our CEO, **Sam Oberly**, is an expert in predictive logistics with a civilian service medal for his logistical coordination algorithm development. He is a published mathematician, trained at Hopkins and Cambridge. (<https://www.linkedin.com/in/sam-oberly/>)

Our CTO, **Abdelrahman Hamimi**, is an AWS certified cloud solutions architect who built internal automation software at GEICO used internally across multiple departments. He graduated from Hopkins with an MS and a BS in computer science, and a BA in Economics. His entire immediate family are doctors. (<https://www.linkedin.com/in/abdelrahman-hamimi-2064ab202/>)

Our COO, **Zachary Dermody**, has boots-on-the-ground experience in logistics management at Amazon and McMaster-Carr. He studied economics and computer science at Hopkins, and his mother is a practicing physician. (<https://www.linkedin.com/in/zachary-dermody-41238a202/>)

launches.title: Aemon — The AI R&D Engineer
launches.tagline: Your next breakthrough. Found automatically.
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

Hi! We're Ray and Richard — twin brothers, and co-founders of [Aemon](https://aemon.ai/).

## TL;DR

Aemon is an AI R&D engineer. Give it a problem and a way to measure success — it reads state-of-the-art research, then generates and evolves thousands of approaches at machine speed to discover optimal solutions, often going beyond what human experts can find.

You say: "Here's my problem. Here's how I measure success. Beat the best known solution."

Aemon is already in the hands of R&D teams, discovering solutions that surpass their existing approaches.

We pointed Aemon at the circle packing problem — a classic NP-hard optimization challenge that mathematicians have worked on for decades.

**Aemon set a new world record. With less than $10 of compute. (see below)**

## 😖 The Problem

Global R&D spend is $3.1 trillion a year. And every R&D problem has the same shape: you know what success looks like, but you don't know how to get there.

Today, that means hiring R&D engineers to read and align papers, pick an approach, implement it, test it, and iterate — by hand. It's slow, it's expensive, and no matter how good your team is, they can only explore a tiny fraction of the solution space. That means the best solution is almost certainly out there, untested, because no human team has the bandwidth to find it.

This isn't a tooling problem. It's a search problem — and humans are the bottleneck.

## 🤓 Our Solution

Aemon does what a world-class R&D engineer does — but at a scale no human team can match.

* **Research synthesis** — Aemon reads state-of-the-art papers to understand what's been tried, what works, and where the frontier is.
* **Autonomous evolution** — It generates and evolves thousands of approaches against your eval, exploring far more of the solution space than any human team could.
* **Expert steerable** — Your team stays in control. A simple direction is all it takes to guide Aemon — constraining the solution space, prioritizing certain approaches, or steering away from dead ends. R&D gets faster and more precise, and Aemon fits into your existing R&D workflow.
* **Beyond state-of-the-art results** — Aemon doesn't just match the best known solution. It looks for better ones — and finds them.

The result: solutions that are validated against your eval, benchmarked against the public state of the art. Your experts stay in the loop — Aemon just gives them superhuman reach. <https://youtu.be/YOswpdEcFUM>

## 🥇 New Record

We pointed Aemon at the circle packing problem — a classic NP-hard optimization challenge that mathematicians have worked on for decades.

Aemon set a new world record. With less than $10 of compute.

It beat Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve with fractional the cost.

Verify it yourself using their official verifier (B.12, n=26): [\[VERIFIER LINK\]](https://colab.research.google.com/github/google-deepmind/alphaevolve_results/blob/master/mathematical_results.ipynb#scrollTo=v3kEu5yVeJ2h) | [Aemon’s Solution](https://aemon.ai/#:~:text=of%20compute-,View,-Aemon%27s%20solution)

## Our Story

We're twins who've been working together our whole lives. We published at ICLR and EMNLP before turning 20, then dropped out of UWaterloo and UIUC to build Aemon full-time. There's a good story behind why we started this — too long for here, but ask us and we'll tell you.

## 🙏 Our Ask

If you are, or know, any of the following, we'd love to talk:

* CTOs, Heads of R&D, or engineering leaders evaluating whether to hire another R&D engineer or want to accelerate R&D.
* Leadership at teams working on any problem where you have a clear eval but no clear path to the best solution
* AI/ML teams trying to be and staying SOTA
* computational teams in fields like quant, finance, biotech, logistics, or materials science where better algorithms directly drive business value

Please reach out to us at [founder@aemon.ai](mailto:founder@aemon.ai) or book a discovery call at [aemon.ai](http://aemon.ai)

launches.title: Ashr: Mimic Your Production Environment and Users to Catch Agent Fails
launches.tagline: Custom Tests and Evals Simulating Real User Behavior
launches.body:
Hi YC, we’re Shreyas and Rohan — two ex-Berkeley students building Ashr.

**TL;DR :** Ashr catches bugs and validates agent response quality by mimicking the patterns and quirks of real users. Developers today struggle to simulate these conditions in tests, resulting in real-time fails and unexpected behavior. We integrate as an SDK within your codebase.

<https://youtu.be/O_sTLTk906E>

# The Problem

AI automations are top of mind for every developer: large companies are integrating AI into older systems to stay technologically relevant, while AI-native companies are quickly emerging in every vertical. Unfortunately, most of these AI tools miss the mark: constant hallucinations, unexpected behavior, and dubious quality have eroded trust in agentic systems. In most cases, this is not because foundation models aren’t powerful enough, but because of subtle prompting, tooling, and scaffolding errors that only emerge with rigorous testing. The need for high volumes of realistic testing arises in many scenarios: we’ve spoken to companies who want to prove that their agents are capable of handling sensitive data to potential customers, developers who want to make their agents work better, and engineers who want to test edge-cases and new features but don’t have all the necessary tools.

We’ve seen teams confront this problem with a litany of half-measures: pushing to production and tanking user trust as a means of discovering bugs, half-baked test harnesses, and vibe-coded test suites that only scratch the surface. We built ashr to solve this.

# Our Solution

Ashr is a modular testing and evaluation platform for your agentic system. We integrate as an SDK into your codebase, allowing you to request test suites and analyzing your agents’ output based off your tooling and ideal outputs. These tests mimic how real users utilize an agentic system: taking complex tool call paths, using obscure language with unclear instructions, and attempting to use restricted features. We develop environments, fine-tuned custom scorers, and stop at nothing to provide all the insights needed to bring your agent to a truly production-ready state.

We also work seamlessly with Claude Code and Cursor, allowing your coding agents to quickly prototype and test changes while receiving immediate feedback. Teams have run swarms of agents testing with ashr overnight, and have woken up to changes that reduced hallucinations and increased accuracy and user retention, all without writing a single line of code.

# Our Ask

If you’re building agents, book a call today at [**https://ashr.io/**](https://ashr.io/). **All onboarding is done via call so we can ensure everyone is ready to go and start using as soon as possible.** In addition, we’d love feedback on our docs, opinions about the nature of test infra, and just chatting with a bunch of builders on how to make our product better.

You can reach us at [founders@ashr.io](mailto:founders@ashr.io)

# The Team

**We’re two young founders passionate about changing the world with agentic development**

* **Rohan** built his first startup, an AI-native survey platform for old age homes, as a student at Berkeley, before exiting as part of an acquisition and joining YC.
* **Shreyas** worked on AI-native workflows at Tessera Labs, mentored by a team of ex-Meta and Netflix research, and delivering value in the ERP transformations of Fortune 100 companies.

name: OctaPulse
long_description:
OctaPulse uses AI vision to automate hatchery QA for fish farms, starting with broodstock phenotyping and juvenile deformity inspection. We cut inspection time from about 5 minutes to under 30 seconds per fish, with more than 90 percent accuracy, so farms advance only high quality fish and waste less feed and labor. Our goal is to bring automation across the entire fish production lifecycle for the $300B aquaculture industry.

Aquaculture is the fastest growing food sector, and has already surpassed commercial fishing for production of seafood. Yet two of the most critical QA and QC steps in fish production are still done by hand: phenotyping and deformity inspection. These processes are slow, error prone, and despised by technicians but vital for the success of the farm, so much so that farms spend >$200K a year on trained technicians and geneticists to operate. We’ve built an AI vision platform for vertically integrated finfish farms that drops into existing workflows starting in the hatchery, uses off the shelf cameras, standardizes these QA steps, and creates a proprietary multi species dataset that becomes the brain for future autonomous aquafarms. Phenotyping is the start, but the platform is designed to be a drop in solution that can easily expand into feeding, health monitoring, and processing so we can solve production problems across the lifecycle.

 We signed a 6-figure paid pilot with the largest trout producer in the United States, are deploying into 2 more farms early 2026, and trained models above 90 percent accuracy while cutting inspection time from 5 minutes to under 30 seconds. Each deployment adds labeled images to our dataset and improves cross species generalization.
one_liner: CV and robotics to automate quality inspection in fish farms

launches.tagline: The future in Space is unfolding
launches.body:
**TL;DR** We’re building deployable solar arrays that expand from the size of a dining table to a football field in orbit. We already have several LOIs from Space companies totaling over $175M and are planning our first in-space demo flight for Q2 2027.

<https://youtu.be/j3FkauBHD8o>

# _The Problem:_

Just like the trunk of your car on a road trip, a rocket ride to space is volume-constrained.

But the critical systems that enable Space services — solar arrays and thermal radiators — get better as they get bigger. Power generation and heat dissipation both require a large surface area, and both must be tightly packed for launch.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/61659d57-59a7-45a9-bb77-aada242bc186)

As space infrastructure scales, power demands per launch are rising fast. That means more watts generated and rejected. Existing deployable structures don’t scale to meet this demand - they’re unreliable, too expensive, take up too much volume, and, importantly for controlling the satellite, too flimsy after deployment.

Power generation and heat dissipation are becoming the limiting factors for larger, more capable spacecraft.

# _The Solution:_

Beyond Reach Labs builds solar panels and thermal radiators for space that grow from the size of a dining table to a football field in orbit, supporting the growing demand for power from orbital data centers, commercial space stations, and lunar outposts.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/d99b0409-8374-4f34-abab-4d7c6de81717)

Our **patented deployable structures** dramatically improve both stowage efficiency and structural stiffness, enabling kilometer-scale systems from a single launch.

We’re starting with deployable solar arrays, where we’ve already secured several multi-million dollar LOIs from customers building next-generation space platforms.

Our first flight demonstration is targeted for late Q2 2027.

# _Why now?_

Power demand in orbit is exploding… scaling from \~**50 Megawatts today to >500 Gigawatts by 2035** (a 10,000x increase), driven by mega-constellations and in-space data centers - and the deployment bottleneck is becoming critical.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/15ea5164-dec9-48a4-a7b9-c29861dde096)

# _Why us?_

**Pele Collins:** \~7 years at SpaceX leading parachute engineering & production, supporting 30+ Dragon missions — designing, qualifying, and flying mission-critical space hardware.

**Dr. Mitchell Fogelson:** PhD from Carnegie Mellon focused on the design, optimization, and simulation of large deployable space structures with NASA - and the inventor of BRL’s core technology.

We’ve been building together since freshman year at UPenn (2013).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/adf86f6f-da51-46d2-a2bb-e5360ca6037f)

# Long-term vision

Near-term: Make deployables boring, trustworthy, and scalable for today’s missions.

Long-term: Enable kilometer-scale space infrastructure — including artificial-gravity stations and persistent human presence in space.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97994&key=user_uploads/3155260/a3ea1c41-9f88-4a88-b78e-4b78f2d8a543)

If this resonates, please reach out to us here: [founders@beyondreachlabs.io](mailto:founders@beyondreachlabs.io)

Website: <https://www.beyondreachlabs.com>

Pele: <https://www.linkedin.com/in/pelecollins/>

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Drone threats have evolved. Detection technology hasn’t and makes lots of mistakes. We solve this with a suite of sensors, including our millimeter-wave radar, purpose-built for the hardest targets. If you’re responsible for countering drone threats, get in touch at [founders@dronetector.com](mailto:founders@dronetector.com).

**The problem**

Small drones are now a security problem. They’re cheap, widely available, and increasingly capable. As a result, they’re showing up in places they shouldn’t – from airports and critical infrastructure to prisons and defense environments.

Detecting them reliably, however, is still a hard problem.

Most drone detection systems weren’t designed for small, low-cost drones. False positives are common, and real threats are missed.

That’s why we’re building [@DroneTector](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/31144).

**Our solution** 

DroneTector provides millimeter-wave radar engineered to detect small drones that others miss. Integrated with our camera and acoustic arrays, we deliver reliable detection against the most challenging targets.

See our technology in action: <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=50xAb06cyq4>

Our sensors can operate as a standalone solution or as part of a distributed detection network. They’re highly scalable, adaptable to complex environments, and able to detect drones that other solutions simply can’t. 

**The team**

We’re a team of PhDs from top UK universities with highly relevant expertise. We’ve been supported by the **UK MoD’s Defence and Security Accelerator**, **NATO DIANA** and the **Royal Academy of Engineering**. 

**Dr Matthew Moore (CEO) -** Matthew holds a PhD from the University of St Andrews, specializing in millimeter-wave radar for drone detection. He has extensive RF engineering experience and is a Royal Academy of Engineering Enterprise Fellow. 

**Dr Thomas Doherty (CTO) -** Thomas holds a PhD from the University of Oxford, and has a decade of experience in optical and laser technologies. He brings engineering physics expertise and is a Royal Academy of Engineering Enterprise Fellow. 

**Dr Jordina Frances de Mas (COO) -** Jordina holds a PhD from the University of St Andrews, focusing on automated reasoning. She brings deep expertise in machine learning and algorithmic optimization.  

**Our ask** 

If you’re responsible for countering the drone threat – **in airports, critical infrastructure, venues, VIP protection, or defense** – we’d love to talk. Contact us at [founders@dronetector.com](mailto:founders@dronetector.com).

launches.tagline: Salus checks your agent's actions, blocking incorrect ones and providing feedback to guide retries
launches.body:
### **TL;DR:**

**Salus is an API that wraps around your agent and checks its actions at runtime, blocking incorrect ones and providing immediate feedback to guide retries.**

We’re Kevin and Vedant, former roommates at Stanford who studied CS, now building Salus full-time.

### 😔**The problem:** 

Your agent processed a refund without looking up the order, costing you thousands. It emailed your top lead using hallucinated data, ruining the deal. You only found out three hours later from a support ticket or an angry email.

Evals, output scoring, and observability are all necessary—but all reactive. They can reduce the likelihood of these problems occurring, but there's no solution that inspects an action as it’s about to execute. Salus does that.

**Ask:** If you are deploying agents and want to improve their correctness we’d love to help. Book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/d/cycy-fbc-fyj/salus-demo), and we can onboard you immediately with just a pip install and a few lines of code.

### 💻 **Our Solution:** 

<https://youtu.be/uyl5NJTY5Cg>

**How Salus validates an action:**

1. Actions must be **grounded in evidence**: Salus maintains an evidence cache for each run that every proposed action is validated against. Evidence includes all outputs from prior tool calls and the entire conversation history.
2. It must **adhere to policy**: Write constraints in YAML, markdown, or plain English. Salus compiles them into runtime checks that are version-controlled, diffable, and shadow-testable
3. And **more**: PII detection, budget/loop protection, idempotency, human-in-the-loop escalation, content moderation

**Self-repairing:** When Salus blocks an action, the agent receives structured feedback to guide a retry. In our benchmarks, **58%** of blocked actions recover and complete the task correctly.

### 📊 **Benchmarks:** 

We tested Salus on τ²-bench and ODCV-Bench. On τ²-bench, agents with Salus follow policies more reliably, at up to **60% lower cost**. On ODCV-Bench, Salus **reduced misalignment by 52%** on average across 12 frontier models (see below).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97574&key=user_uploads/1940292/e48b27f6-2e13-4d40-a9a4-13135ff981bc)

### ➕ **Other Features:** 

While we believe the missing piece is runtime validation, we know **evals and observability** are crucial. That’s why we incorporate all three in **one centralized product**. Using templates and LLMs, we generate thousands of both adversarial and realistic evals that have full context of your agent’s domain.

Contact us: [founders@usesalus.ai](https://founders@usesalus.ai)

**2 minute demo -** <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pEfhqhylS2Y>

**What We Learned**

Working on back office document automation, we kept hearing the same questions:

* _"How do I know this workflow will actually work before I bet my ops on it?"_
* _"I aim to have 100 workflows. How will I monitor them all?"_
* _"Can this run in our cloud? Data can't leave our infrastructure."_
* _"Our files have contracts, amendments, and extensions that reference each other. Can you piece that together?"_

Traditional automation tools were built for deterministic processes and they're not designed for AI. AI is a game changer for document processing, but businesses still can't trust it at scale. Why? Evals and monitoring aren't built in. And most new platforms can't run on-prem.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97202&key=user_uploads/2221380/d651a1db-2002-456e-9c18-55d290083745)

**The Solution: A Platform Where You Can Trust AI Workflows**

EigenPal is built around one principle: like any employees you entrust work to, you need to trust your workflows before you deploy them and monitor them after.

* **Agentic workflow builder.** Our AI workflow builder let’s you create workflows with easy in your natural language. It can even iterate on a workflow on a test dataset to tune accuracy.
* **Eval-first.** Before any workflow goes live, test it against your historical documents. See exactly what accuracy you're getting. Deploy only when you're confident. **Set up a feedback loop in production** so workflows are adjusted with feedback.
* **Document-centric.** Upload files directly, no public URLs needed. Built-in storage plus a powerful template filler to generate polished output docs from your extracted data.
* **Configure everything.** Choose your OCR/VLM, LLM, configure every step of the pipeline separately. Access built-in tracing for workflows in our app or export via OpenTelemetry.
* **Monitor hundreds of workflows at once.** One dashboard showing costs, compliance logs, and failures across every workflow. Know immediately when something drifts.
* **Collaborate with your team.** Org workspaces let you share workflows, templates, and results with colleagues. Build once, use across your team.
* **On-prem or cloud.** Runs in your infrastructure with your LLMs, or use our hosted version. Your choice.

launches.tagline: Fern joins every meeting as–either invisible copilot or active participant–so every conversation runs like a top 1% professional
launches.body:
**TL;DR**\
[Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) is a realtime AI that joins your meetings as either an invisible copilot or an active participant– your choice! It realtime proactively coaches you through every conversation so you always show up like a top 1% professional.

Hey everyone, we're Amit and Robert, cofounders of Ishiki Labs.

**The Problem**

_“AI meeting assistant” has become synonymous with a note-taker waiting to summarize at the end. That's not a meeting assistant. That's a fancier transcript._ 

Building a realtime AI meeting copilot is hard in two distinct ways.

The invisible assistant must understand the live meeting context at blazing speed and surface the right thing at the right moment – questions to ask, things you're missing, who you're talking to. Timing is everything. Current AI is purely reactive. Making AI an active participant in discussion is even harder. AI has no social awareness – every pause becomes a prompt, every gap an invitation to speak.

AI that is socially aware and proactive is an unsolved problem. That's what we're building.

The cost of this gap is real. Cofounders, AEs, recruiters, investors – in discovery calls, sales meetings, investor conversations. The moments that matter most, and AI is absent from all of them.

**How Fern Solves it**

[Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) joins your meetings as a true participant or an invisible copilot – your choice. It has two modes:

**Full Presence**: Fern joins visibly, listens, and speaks up when invited. It offers realtime opinions, deep research, and can complete tasks like filing notes or sending emails on the spot. Built for internal product, engineering, and strategy meetings. Watch the demo- <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vRJfZDUHvSY>

**Shadow Mode**: Silent and invisible to everyone else. You get a private realtime feed: live summaries, questions to ask, things you're missing, context on who you're talking to. A sharp colleague whispering in your ear – with fully customizable insights. Built for client calls, investor meetings, and any conversation where you want invisible support.

Both modes include a post-meeting summary, transcript, and full insights.

**Team**

We're both ex-Meta. Amit is an AI Scientist from LLaMA (now Meta Super Intelligence Lab) and Reality Labs – PhD in AI, 20+ publications at NeurIPS/CVPR, trained multimodal assistants for smart glasses. Robert was systems and infra lead in Reality Labs, with four years building low-latency multimodal systems at Meta and Citadel Securities. 

Our mission: make AI socially timed and contextually aware – so every conversation you have runs like a top 1% professional.

**Our Ask**

Download [Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) and if you're a founder or AE who lives in high-stakes conversations and don’t want to settle for AI note-takers, reach out: [team@ishikilabs.ai](mailto:team@ishikilabs.ai)

**TL;DR:** APIs weren’t built for agents, we fixed that. Developers and agents get instant access to hundreds of APIs through our MCP or SDK. No key management, no billing headaches, pay as you go. API providers list once and become instantly discoverable. 

_Ask:_ We’d love an intro to teams building agents to understand how they’re handling paid APIs today. Contact us at [founders@orthogonal.com](mailto:founders@orthogonal.com)

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CixNTItWDjI>

**The Problem:**

AI agents are about to become the biggest consumers of APIs on the internet. But they struggle to access tools.

MCP helped standardize tool calling, but created fragmentation. Some services have MCPs, others don't. Some map to single APIs, others wrap entire workflows. Agents end up with 30+ tools, bloating context.

Worse, any MCP requiring identity or payment means managing accounts, API keys, billing, and auth across dozens of services. And most APIs don't even have MCPs.

You could have your agent find APIs, sign up, handle auth, and buy credits, but the failure rate is high. The entire API economy was built for humans.

Meanwhile, API providers are leaving money on the table. Billions of agents could be paying for their APIs right now, but they have no way to find or transact with them.

These APIs are locked behind API keys and human payment methods, which agents do not have access to.

**The Solution:**

Orthogonal is where agents go to find and pay for APIs.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Terranox AI ([terranox.ai](http://terranox.ai)) is the first vertically integrated AI-powered uranium discovery company. We discover economic uranium deposits in North America using AI trained on 70+ years of exploration outcomes. Our mission is to find the fuel we need to power the next century with nuclear energy.

<https://youtu.be/2R8vyyOSH0A>

⚡️ **The Nuclear Renaissance:**

Nuclear is experiencing a global resurgence as the only scalable clean baseload power option that can meet humanity's exploding energy needs:

* **AI datacenter electricity demand** will more than double by 2030
* Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta have collectively **committed billions to nuclear power**
* 30+ countries pledged to **more than triple global nuclear capacity by 2050**
* In 2025, the U.S. government signed executive orders to **quadruple nuclear capacity**, with $80B+ in commitments across reactors and fuel supply chains

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98155&key=user_uploads/898324/f98faf46-f9ae-4a9b-b299-2fbbd1361db4)

⛽️ **The Fuel Crisis:**

But this nuclear future has one critical dependency: **uranium fuel.**

* Global uranium production needs to **4x by 2050**, but we already have a **supply deficit today** with depleting stockpiles
* The world’s largest mines will **approach end-of-life** simultaneously starting in the mid 2030s
* New mines take **10-15 years from discovery to production**

**The West needs new economic discoveries in stable jurisdictions to ensure energy security.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98155&key=user_uploads/854295/8b02b13f-eeba-4933-a331-5a6556f57c7a)

🆘 **The Bottleneck: Exploration is Broken**

Exploration still works like in the 1960s: slow, fragmented, guided by intuition and outsourced workflows. **Hit rates are <1%**, driving extremely high costs and decade-long timelines. Meanwhile, 70+ years of exploration data sits trapped in thousands of legacy PDFs and handdrawn maps, unused.

**We're not finding deposits fast enough to power the future.**

⚒️ **What We Are Building:**

**Terranox AI is the first vertically integrated AI-powered uranium discovery company.**

We find uranium deposits in North America using AI trained on decades of geoscience data and exploration outcomes.

**Our system does three things:**

1. **Multi-modal geoscience intelligence:** Extracts and processes geoscience data from decades of fragmented sources, building a unified exploration context base
2. **Prospectivity mapping for discovery:** Identifies high-potential areas humans would miss using uranium-specific AI models trained on decades of exploration outcomes
3. **Sequential decision intelligence:** Determines the optimal next action to maximize information gain per dollar spent, learning from every result in real time

**The result:** A compounding learning flywheel. Every drill hole (hit or miss) makes our predictions better across all projects. The more we explore, the smarter we get.

We're launching our own exploration projects in North America to ensure the nuclear renaissance has the fuel it needs.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98155&key=user_uploads/854295/21570b8b-dce2-4a8b-8340-7409fc467ab0)

👷‍♀️👷‍♂️ **Who We Are:**

**Jade Checlair - CEO & Co-Founder**

PhD Geophysics (UChicago). Developed statistical methods for planetary discovery adopted by NASA flagship missions. 3.5 years at BCG leading nuclear and mining strategy. Ex-NASA Ames.

**Leeav Lipton - CTO & Co-Founder**

8 years building AI/ML systems at Borealis AI. Astrophysics background. Ex-NASA JPL scientist on low-cost remote sensing tech.

We met in first-year physics and have been friends for 10+ years.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98155&key=user_uploads/898324/4ee78148-0515-4578-ad43-c07e2754d020)

Contact us at [founders@terranox.ai](mailto:founders@terranox.ai).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9Db70ieMYkA>

**The Problem:**

Long-running agents are starting to handle complex tasks entirely on their own. They can plan, execute, and complete multi-step workflows without human intervention. But that autonomy ends the moment a payment is involved, because transactions still require a human to manually enter payment details and authorize the charge.

**The Solution:**

To solve this, Sponge built infrastructure that lets agents handle payments on their own.

**Sponge Wallet** enables agents to sign up and pay for services without human involvement. Users fund their wallet once, and agents autonomously use those funds to pay for what it needs.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97911&key=user_uploads/300418/a9904dc0-f667-4060-9697-e78f4a955155)

**Sponge Gateway** enables businesses to sell directly to agents. Businesses can upload their API spec and allow agents to onboard and pay for usage autonomously, without requiring a human to give a credit card or an API key. No code changes required.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97911&key=user_uploads/300418/0c13e43e-b0b7-4400-9c8c-79408aa9eaba)

As agents become increasingly autonomous and begin making decisions on their own, they need financial primitives to operate like humans. We’re building the infrastructure that makes this possible.

**Our Ask:**

If you use agents (such as OpenClaw), add our [wallet skill](https://sponge.md) to let them sign up and pay for services autonomously. If you're a business, upload your API spec to [gateway.paysponge.com](http://gateway.paysponge.com) to start onboarding agents and selling to them directly, without human involvement.

**The Team:**

We're a team of ex-Stripe tech leads that built Stripe's stablecoin financial accounts, stablecoin payments and core money movement systems for humans. We are now bringing those learnings to build out the financial infrastructure for the next economic actors: agents.

**To give your agent an account or to sell to agents, visit [paysponge.com](http://paysponge.com) or contact [team@paysponge.com](mailto:team@paysponge.com).**

30 million orthopedic surgeries are conducted every year, that all receive some form of medical imaging prior to surgery. \

While modern AI excels in any area you can collect a lot of data for, it struggles in areas where data is sparse or costly to attain. Designing new molecules, discovering new physics, and engineering new materials are all domains where collecting data is extremely costly. 

We dream of a world where AI accelerates research in all of these domains and creates a more abundant future for humanity, but the current technology is not there. That’s why we started Confluence Labs. 

We are building AI that can design highly effective experiments in data-sparse domains and learn maximally from the data it already has.

launches.body:
Confluence Labs is coming out of stealth with **SOTA on ARC-AGI-2** with a score of **97.9%** at \~$12 per task on the public eval. This is how we did it, why it matters, and what's next.

ARC-AGI-2 is a benchmark that tests an AI system's ability to solve novel reasoning tasks from just a few examples. It's considered one of the hardest AI benchmarks in the world. As recently as a year ago, even the best models scored in the single digits.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98111&key=user_uploads/1164255/2f4e4c89-6f96-48ca-93ea-a84eccc15092)

We've open sourced our SOTA solver. You can reproduce our results here: <https://github.com/confluence-labs/arc-agi-2>.

**Our Approach – Program Synthesis driven by LLMs**

LLMs are exceedingly good at writing code. We take the latest models and allow them to find the optimal solution by directing them to write code which describes the transformation represented by a particular ARC problem.

The principles of our approach can be boiled down to a few key ideas:

1\. Structure the problem such that it optimally resembles the underlying LLM's training data

2\. Enable long-horizon work on the problem so a model can continue to build on its past work

3\. Precisely structure the criteria of the solution and give the model a way to measure that

**ARC-AGI-2 is Saturated – What Does This Mean for the World?**

ARC is a data efficiency benchmark. It measures how well you can make a prediction based on a few examples. Typical approaches to ARC-AGI have struggled because modern ML excels in areas where you can collect a lot of training data, but struggles in areas where data is sparse or costly to attain.

We think LLMs can be used in combination with discrete modeling to assist humans in data-sparse domains. We're most excited about the application of this to meaningful and challenging frontiers such as hardware engineering, drug design, and physics research.

**What Does This Mean for Us?**

Our core belief is that learning efficiency is the key bottleneck to solving the world's hardest problems. We think AI can help in data-sparse domains, and we're approaching this from 2 angles:

1\. **Hypothesis generation** – A hypothesis is a testable prediction about the world. If you optimally generate hypotheses, the results of your experiments are maximally informative, and you can reduce the time it takes to develop a new technology or solve a hard problem.

2\. **Data-Efficient Modeling** – By pushing the capabilities of both LLMs and discrete program search, we can make predictions with far less data and accelerate frontier research.

**What's Next?**

We're going hard on developing our core technology, building out the team, and developing partnerships with researchers and engineers. We're looking for collaborators in hardware engineering, biology, materials science, and other fields where progress is gated by the cost of physical experiments. If that sounds like you or someone you know, reach out at [founders@confluence.sh](mailto:founders@confluence.sh).

launches.body:
One of the hardest things to scale in healthcare is also one of the most basic: making sure patients and clinicians actually understand each other.

**TL;DR**: [Opalite](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/opalite-health) helps healthcare providers communicate with patients who don't speak English with an AI medical interpreter that saves 20% time per session and millions annually on interpretation costs.

Launch Video: <https://youtu.be/_AMvW9Co9do?si=YTKM4wGUgz0-qmrs>


**🤯 The Problem**

When patients and providers don't speak the same language, critical medical information gets lost - symptoms are misunderstood, diagnoses are wrong, and patients can't follow treatment plans. 

Over 30 million people in the US have limited English proficiency, and these communication breakdowns lead to worse outcomes across nearly every measure. Federal law requires healthcare providers to offer interpretation to solve this, but the current solution - a human medical interpreter - doesn't work. 

Getting an interpreter takes up to 30 minutes, if one is available at all. When they do connect, interpreters frequently omit or mistranslate important details, especially in fast-moving or complex visits. It also costs hospitals upwards of $1-2M per year. The system is expensive, slow, and unreliable, creating gaps in communication that put patients at risk and increase liability for healthcare organizations.


**❤️ The Solution** 

Opalite is an AI-powered medical interpreter that helps healthcare professionals communicate with non-English-speaking patients. It’s available instantly, 24/7, so care doesn't have to wait for an interpreter to connect.

Opalite works directly inside clinical workflows, including the EHR, allowing providers to communicate in real time without switching tools or interrupting visits. Translation quality is proven to be superior to certified medical interpreters, but at more than 50% lower cost than traditional services. Opalite also generates visit documentation automatically, reducing the amount of charting providers need to do after each encounter.


**📊 Our progress:** 

Opalite is currently used daily by patients and providers across 10+ states. Our customers include hospitals, community health centers, home health organizations, telehealth providers, and clinics. We are also set to roll out in a large healthcare enterprise within the next two months. 


**💡 Our Story**

[@Cathleen Kuo](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/1543800) is a physician and the child of immigrants who don't speak English. She has seen the language barrier issues from both sides - watching her parents struggle to communicate with their doctors, and later experiencing firsthand how language barriers compromise the care she can deliver as a physician.

[@Alex Mehregan](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/657915) is a former software engineer at Apple where he worked on Apple Intelligence and the updated Siri - software that touches many millions of users every day. He is a 2x founder and Berkeley EECS alumni.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97038&key=user_uploads/1543800/8c237420-8e5d-47b5-8721-05769cabb1d9)

* Have experience with medical interpreters (as a provider or patient)? Your feedback would be invaluable.

**Reach out at**: [cathleen@opalitehealth.com](mailto:cathleen@opalitehealth.com) & [alex@opalitehealth.com](mailto:alex@opalitehealth.com)

**Visit us**: <https://opalitehealth.com>

launches.title: IncidentFox. The AI SRE who never drops context.
launches.tagline: Auto-learns your stack, builds its own integrations, and gets smarter after every incident.
launches.body:
Hey everyone 👋

We're [Long](https://www.linkedin.com/in/long-yi-b221b2183/) and [Jimmy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chiehmin-wei/) — co-founders of IncidentFox.

**TL;DR**

AI SRE tools fail without deep context about _your_ systems — and that context lives in integrations nobody has time to build. IncidentFox auto-discovers what each team needs, generates the integrations, and ships with 300+ tools built in. Setup takes less than a day, not months.

👉 Try it: <https://incidentfox.ai>

👉 Open source (Apache 2.0): <https://github.com/incidentfox/incidentfox>

👉 Launch video: <https://youtu.be/TaTpN0JwNYE>

**❌ The Problem: Without the right integrations, your AI has no context**

Every AI SRE tool connects to Slack, reads your Confluence, queries your Datadog. That part is solved.

Here's what isn't: when the AI actually needs to debug something, it doesn't have the right tools.

Your payments team runs a custom Kafka pipeline with internal dashboards. Your infra team uses a homegrown deployment system. Your ML team has proprietary model serving. Each team's stack is different — and the AI has no way to query any of it.

The traditional fix? Hand-build integrations (MCP servers) for every team.

But this creates a new problem:

* Who decides what integrations each team needs? You might know your own team's stack — but when you're debugging another team's service at 3 AM, you don't know theirs.
* So every team needs to sacrifice an engineer to build and maintain their own integrations. That's expensive, slow, and doesn't scale.
* Most teams never get around to it. The AI stays half-useful.

**Integration is the bottleneck.** Not the AI model. Not the monitoring data. The integrations.

**🦊 IncidentFox: We auto-build the integrations for you**

IncidentFox is an AI SRE that lives where your team already works — Slack, Microsoft Teams, or Google Chat. It doesn't just connect to your existing tools — it figures out what tools each team needs and builds them automatically.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/102ebfb0-a3c9-45c5-b993-89e39b94e13b)

**1. Auto-discovers and generates integrations**

IncidentFox analyzes your codebase, infrastructure, and incident history to identify gaps — then auto-generates the tools to fill them. No engineer needs to hand-build MCP servers. No team needs to sacrifice headcount on integration work.

A new team onboards? IncidentFox studies their stack and proposes tools specific to their services — with human approval before anything goes live.

**2. Per-team configuration — because every team is different**

Your payments team and your ML team don't use the same stack. Why would they use the same AI SRE config?

Each team gets their own:

* Tools — enable only what's relevant; disable what isn't
* Prompts — fully open source and exposed to engineers. Inject your domain knowledge directly
* Knowledge base — learned from that team's incidents, runbooks, and services

One team's "config drift" is another team's "model drift." IncidentFox understands the difference.

**3. Continuously evaluates and self-improves**

After every incident, IncidentFox:

* Detects gaps — "I couldn't query service X's health endpoint"
* Auto-generates the missing tool
* Evaluates its own investigation quality against the actual resolution
* Updates prompts and knowledge — with human review

It gets measurably better every week. Not because you tuned it — because it tuned itself.

**4. 300+ integrations included on day one**

While it auto-builds what's missing, you're not starting from zero. Kubernetes, AWS, Grafana, Prometheus, Datadog, Elasticsearch, PagerDuty, GitHub — all built in. Integration time is under a day, not months.

**🧠 Why this matters**

**Integrations** — Traditional: Hand-built per team. Each team sacrifices an engineer. IncidentFox: Auto-discovered and auto-generated. Human approves.

**Multi-team scaling** — Traditional: Breaks — you can't know every team's stack. IncidentFox: Per-team config. Each team's AI knows their stack.

**Domain knowledge** — Traditional: Black box prompts, hope it works. IncidentFox: Open source prompts. Engineers inject and edit freely.

**Over time** — Traditional: Stagnates unless manually updated. IncidentFox: Self-evaluates, finds gaps, improves continuously.

**Setup** — Traditional: Months of custom integration work. IncidentFox: < 1 day. 300+ tools out of the box.

**📊 Results**

* 85–95% reduction in alert noise through intelligent correlation
* Hours → minutes for incident investigation
* Zero-config onboarding — Docker in 5 min, production K8s in 30 min

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/844d70ec-e308-472c-9bc4-f212cd954153)

**🔒 Enterprise-ready, open-source**

* Open source — Apache 2.0, no vendor lock-in
* SOC 2 compliant, SSO/OIDC, RBAC, audit logs
* Self-hosted, on-prem, or managed SaaS
* Bring your own LLM keys (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, etc.)

**👬 The Team**

[**Jimmy (CEO)**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chiehmin-wei/) — Previously at Roblox, where he built social communication features (in-experience calling for 100M+ DAU). Before that, worked at Meta FAIR on multiparty conversational AI, with published research. Cornell CS. Serial founder — previously CTO at a startup in Outlier Ventures' DeFi accelerator.

[**Long (CTO)** ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/long-yi-b221b2183/)— Previously at Roblox, where he built database infrastructure supporting 100M+ daily active users on the Stateful Infra team. Experienced the chaos of on-call firsthand — which is why we're building this. Brandeis CS + Neuroscience + Business.

We've lived on both sides: Jimmy built the AI systems, Long was the SRE drowning in incidents. IncidentFox is what happens when you combine both.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97928&key=user_uploads/1146198/261f0711-50aa-4a0f-b6c9-9cdc7c853dbc)


**🙏 Our Asks**

* Try IncidentFox — self-serve at [incidentfox.ai](https://incidentfox.ai) or star us on [GitHub](https://github.com/incidentfox/incidentfox)
* Intros to engineering teams spending too much time on on-call
  * [Book a demo with us](https://calendly.com/d/cxd2-4hb-qgp/30-minute-demo-call-w-incidentfox)

Thanks for reading ❤️

launches.title: Stilta: Cursor for Patent Practitioners
launches.tagline: AI agents for deep patent research
launches.body:
**_TL;DR:_** Innovation is moving faster than ever, but the tools to protect it aren’t keeping up. We’re building Cursor for patent practitioners, reducing manual research and analysis while unlocking new opportunities.\
\
Know any patent practitioners? Let’s connect: [founders@stilta.com](https://mailto:founders@stilta.com)

[🎥 Watch our launch video](https://youtu.be/lOwJlK1fJLg)

### **Problem**

Missing the right patent, or getting the analysis wrong, can cost billions. That’s why patent practitioners spend a large share of their time reading technical documents and building arguments. LLMs can generate text, but patent work has non-negotiables that most tools still don’t meet.

* **Research is manual:** practitioners spend hours searching and analyzing to find the few patents that matter
* **Tools produce static reports:** most solutions generate a final document or flat lists instead of interactive, argument-led analysis that adapts
* **Context gets lost:** teams lack flexible end-to-end tools, resulting in a fragmented and clunky software stack
* **AI isn’t trusted without evidence:** in patent work, outputs must be traceable to specific references with clear rationale

# **Solution**

We've built Cursor for patent practitioners, using agentic AI to improve how high-stakes patent work is done end-to-end. Our agentic approach works alongside you, iterating on analysis rather than producing one-time reports. Specialized agents with deep domain and skills expertise handle complex patent analysis while building context from your documents and prior work. This enables deeper and more granular analysis that was not previously technically feasible.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97649&key=user_uploads/2960868/ba4d323e-fee5-4a6a-bd58-676deac4f4e8)

Whether you're searching for prior art, analyzing portfolios, or monitoring for infringement, you get interactive litigation analysis you can build on - not flat lists. We're already live with leading firms in both Europe and the US.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97649&key=user_uploads/2960868/c5dff588-5fbb-4681-8cdc-83f577932775)

### **Why this matters**

Innovation is key to solving the world’s biggest challenges, but protecting innovation is still slowed down by manual, fragmented workflows. Patent practitioners should be able to move at the pace of innovation, so great ideas turn into durable competitive advantage.

### **Who we are**

We’re four engineers and previous founders who met at McKinsey/QuantumBlack and spent the last few years building and deploying AI for large organizations. We saw first hand how the IP world has one of the largest gaps between available tools and what's needed - the perfect match for what we've built our expertise to solve.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97649&key=user_uploads/2960868/769e1ba6-fde1-4ff9-83b9-16509abf0b5a)

* [Tobias ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tobiasestreen/)previously led AI projects at QuantumBlack and Netlight (and once turned down a pro League of Legends contract).
* [Petrus ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/petruswerner/)is a builder who’s spent the past 5 years scaling AI systems at QuantumBlack and AWS.
* [Oskar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/oskarblock/) founded and bootstrapped two startups to +$1M ARR in parallel to working at McKinsey & Goldman Sachs.
* [Oscar ](https://www.linkedin.com/in/oscaradamsson/)competed nationally in Math, lead product development at unicorns, and worked with +50 CEOs at McKinsey.

### **Our ask**

If you know patent practitioners who'd benefit from faster, better, and more interactive research, we'd love an intro. \
\
[Visit our website](https://stilta.com/) | [Contact us](https://mailto:founders@stilta.com) | [Book a demo](https://stilta.cal.eu/stilta/demo)

AI turns this organizational capacity into software.

As institutional advantages become widely accessible, the edge concentrates in each trader’s worldview, judgment, and bets. 

The first one-person investment firm managing $1 billion will emerge within two years.

It will run on Instinct.

launches.title: Cajal: Scaling Formal Verification for Scientific Discovery
launches.tagline: Cajal deploys AI mathematicians to high-impact applied domains, starting with quantum computing and finance.
launches.body:
**TL;DR: Formal verification** uses mathematical proofs to guarantee a system behaves as intended.  Cajal is **massively scaling this technology** with AI - deploying agents to autonomously discover and **formalize new tools** across applied mathematics with genuine real world impact. Starting with **quantum computing and finance.**\
\
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7McsRwyWBNE>

**LLMs: The State of Play**

Large language models are fundamentally stochastic. No amount of scaling changes this - probabilistic systems cannot guarantee correctness. This is especially problematic in mission-critical domains that require mathematical certainty.

Formal verification provides exactly this: mathematical proof that code is correct for every possible input, not just the ones you test. 

Previously, this technology has been limited to a small group of experts working over long horizons - restricting its application to narrow domains like software verification and research mathematics.

**A New Frontier for Formal Verification**

Cajal is using AI to massively scale this technology - deploying agents to autonomously discover and formalize tools across applied science, beginning with quantum computing and finance.

**Introducing Tau:** Tau is a multi-agent system that collaborates to discover and verify new mathematical proofs in Lean. Given a research direction, Tau autonomously formalizes large corpora of applied mathematics, discovering novel results with real-world applications - from algorithms with certified speedups to certificates that a system satisfies its constraints.

Every result is machine-verified by Lean's type-checking kernel, guaranteeing correctness.

**Our Ask**\
Alongside our work formalizing applied mathematics, we also partner with frontier AI labs and research institutes to improve their systems, including through datasets, evals, and RL environments. To explore a collaboration, contact us at [hi@caj.al](mailto:hi@caj.al).

→ [Luke](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lukerjohnston/) and [Pedro](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pedronobree/) from [Cajal](https://caj.al/)

name: Overshoot
long_description:
Overshoot makes it easy for developers to build and run real-time vision applications.

AI can see and understand the physical world. This unlocks new applications in physical security, safety, gaming, robotics and general consumer products. Soon, video agents will watch your home and your pet when you’re away. 

However, existing platforms make it painful for developers to build these real-time applications. Slow inference. Limited model availability. Break at scale. 

Overshoot solves this.

Today, 300+ developers connect live video feeds to the largest collection of Vision Language Models with 3 lines of code. And get responses in less than 200ms. 10x faster than any existing inference platform. Zero infra headache. 

Our moat is focus. Image and Video are fundamentally different modalities from text. By focusing on them, we are able to make strong technical leaps from codec, streaming protocols to inference engines.

Younes and Zakaria are cousins. Zakaria graduated top of his class at LSE and MIT, and later built low-latency high-throughput pricing systems (surge) at Uber and inference engines at Meta. He previously built and sold a software product and won several prominent AI hackathons. Younes was a founding engineer at Cosmonio (later acquired by Intel). He built a training and serving Computer Vision platform from scratch. He witnessed firsthand customers abandoning traditional Computer Vision because it lacked the “general” intelligence LLMs have today. Together we’ve shipped large-scale systems and know where they break.
one_liner: AI Infra for real-time vision applications

We're[ @Huzaifa Ahmad](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ahmadhuzaifa012/),[ @Ahmad Khan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ahmad-khan-b6584b225/), and[ @Prama Yudhistira](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pramayudhistira/) (Parameter W26). **We built AI agents that automate penetration testing.**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97640&key=user_uploads/507733/e0895a51-0f41-4ecb-b7d2-6e10257676ee)

**In the past few weeks, our agents found critical vulnerabilities in dozens of YC companies (ones you’ve heard of):** SQL injection exposing billions of records, demonstrated a PoC worm that could infect entire networks, gained access to hundreds of codebases, and more. Through this, we have prevented an estimated $3B+ in potential damages (based on exposed record counts and IBM's Cost of a Data Breach benchmarks).

[🎥 Watch our launch video](https://youtu.be/kDWcB4GjzeA)

**The problem:** Companies lose $10T+ annually to preventable vulnerabilities, yet most pentest once a year because it's manual, expensive, and slow. By the time you get the PDF, your codebase has changed.

And that gap is widening. In September 2025, Anthropic caught Chinese state-sponsored hackers using AI to run 80-90% of an attack autonomously — thousands of requests per second, speeds no human team could match. The attackers have AI now, and defenders need it too.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97640&key=user_uploads/2947591/e8003001-ba20-41f7-9c96-11922c602f4b)

**What we built:** AI agents that run continuous penetration tests against your apps and infrastructure. They find vulnerabilities, chain exploits together, and deliver actionable findings with reproduction steps — at a fraction of the cost of traditional pentesting.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97640&key=user_uploads/2947591/0f00074f-e1d6-4ef2-bc4e-9466839fab36)

launches.title: Pax Historia - User & AI powered gaming platform
launches.tagline: 🗺️ The first alternate-history sandbox game powered by AI
launches.body:
Hey! This is **Eli** and **Ryan**, cofounders at **Pax Historia** ([paxhistoria.co](http://paxhistoria.co)). 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97520&key=user_uploads/1382898/f7de4ff4-c0d2-4a10-9785-d2ca30e30949)

Pax Historia is a map-based gaming platform which combines the creative freedom of sandbox games with the depth of grand strategy. Players imagine scenarios (like ‘What if the USSR hadn’t broken apart?’ or ‘What if a zombie outbreak started in 2019?’ or ‘What if the USA took over Greenland?’) and create maps and presets which are then published to the community and become playable by anyone.

Already, we have **35k daily users**. Over the last week, in total, we’ve processed **100+ billion tokens**. Our **passionate community has published over 4k presets** with 50+ plays each.  

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97520&key=user_uploads/1382898/099acb66-577a-4be7-973c-109c16087c69)

Creators create, edit, and publish custom maps and worlds. Users then play as a country or group in the world. They can make actions, start diplomatic chats, and jump forward in time. As the game progresses, the map shows any changes from player actions. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97520&key=user_uploads/1382898/062a68cf-5178-40bf-888d-e31b681431c2)

By using AI to power the responses of other countries/actors to in-game actions, **we are able to move beyond constraining, pre-designed narrative paths**. Players are truly able to do whatever they can imagine. 

Check out our [Pax Historia Launch Video](https://youtu.be/-RXSxMVLcL4) for a closer look.

**Our asks**: 

1. **Feedback:** We would _love_ to hear your feedback (especially if you’re a grand strategy, history, or gaming nerd!). You can make an account [here](http://paxhistoria.co).
2. **Talent:** We are hiring! If you know of any talented engineers (Unity, web dev, AI/ML) who might be interested in a super high-impact, fast moving, small team, then please connect us. They can apply through our [Ashby](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/pax-historia), but please also shoot us an email ([careers@paxhistoria.co](mailto:careers@paxhistoria.co)) so we can find their profile.
3. **Connection & Community:** Finally, if you’re running platforms/marketplaces, who are using AI to power features within their service (not just to write code!), or just excited by building and maintaining online communities, then we would love to chat.
